# SEO Content

Create pages for people with a real question or task. Search visibility is a distribution outcome; it does not justify thin pages, unsupported claims, or writing for a keyword score.

## Establish the page decision

Identify:

- the business and user outcome;
- the intended reader and search situation;
- the query or topic and likely intent;
- whether an existing page already serves that intent;
- the project's unique evidence, experience, data, product insight, or examples;
- the next useful action after the reader gets the answer.

Decide whether to create a page, improve an existing page, consolidate overlapping pages, or avoid the topic. Do not recommend a new page when the project has no useful contribution or when an existing page should be strengthened instead.

## Research before prescribing

When current search results or platform guidance affect the decision, inspect them rather than relying on memory. Use primary sources for claims and official documentation for search mechanics. Treat keyword volume, difficulty, competitor structure, and SERP features as evidence—not universal thresholds or mandatory templates.

Separate:

- verified facts from the project or sources;
- reasonable inferences that must be labeled;
- missing information that requires a placeholder or narrower claim.

Never invent firsthand experience, expert review, customer results, citations, statistics, or product comparisons.

## Build the SEO strategy

For each proposed page or cluster, specify:

- audience and search intent;
- the question or task it resolves;
- the unique value the project can add;
- page type and relationship to existing pages;
- evidence and sources required;
- internal links that genuinely help navigation;
- conversion or next step appropriate to the intent;
- how usefulness and business value will be reviewed.

Prefer a small number of strong pages over a large inventory of near-duplicates. Do not create doorway pages, location or comparison pages with only substituted terms, or mass-produced content that adds no original value.

## Turn strategy into todos

Make each todo produce a reviewable artifact, for example:

- intent and source brief for one page;
- rewrite of a specific section;
- complete draft with citations and claim notes;
- internal-link changes with source and destination pages;
- title and description options for one page;
- consolidation or redirect brief;
- post-publication review using named search and conversion signals.

Include the page, evidence source, intended result, required output, and completion check. Avoid vague work such as “do keyword research” or “improve SEO.”

## Write the page

Answer the primary intent early, then provide the detail needed to act. Use headings that describe the content rather than mechanically repeating a phrase. Add examples, comparisons, steps, visuals, or limitations only when they improve understanding.

Create:

- a descriptive title that distinguishes the page;
- a useful search description when requested, without promising that it will always be shown;
- a clear heading structure;
- accurate internal and external links;
- authorship, sourcing, dates, and structured data only when truthful and relevant;
- a CTA matched to the reader's stage.

There is no universal title formula, keyword density, article length, or number of headings. Do not pad content to hit a word count. Do not change dates merely to appear fresh.

## Apply technical recommendations carefully

Recommend canonicals, redirects, indexing controls, sitemaps, or structured data only when they solve a defined issue. Keep structured data consistent with visible content and current eligibility rules. Distinguish discoverability and crawling mechanisms from ranking guarantees. Do not claim that a submission protocol, schema type, or AI-specific markup guarantees Google visibility or citation.

## Revise and consolidate

When revising, preserve supported facts and fix the named weakness: intent mismatch, weak evidence, unclear structure, duplication, stale information, or poor conversion path. Consolidate competing pages when one stronger resource better serves the same intent. If a requested tactic conflicts with current spam policies, explain the risk and propose a people-first alternative.

## Check before delivery

Confirm that:

- the page helps the intended reader complete a real task;
- claims, citations, experience, and comparisons are supported;
- the project contributes something beyond a generic summary;
- the draft does not rely on repetition, hidden text, link schemes, doorway patterns, or scaled unoriginal output;
- on-page elements are accurate and internally consistent;
- current search and structured-data requirements are verified when implementation depends on them.

Use current official guidance when search behavior matters:

- Search Essentials: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials
- Helpful, reliable, people-first content: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content
- Spam policies: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies
- AI features and your website: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide
